The exact five-bit count and the coset obstruction at every dimension

For a uniform five-bit permutation the exact probability of failing to mix on pairs is

2714131451817586666178740224032!=353425151998476166334264020623061220992000000=1.03147600769480393…×10−7. \frac{27\,141\,314\,518\,175\,866\,661\,787\,402\,240}{32!} =\frac{3\,534\,251\,519\,984\,761\,663} {34\,264\,020\,623\,061\,220\,992\,000\,000} =1.03147600769480393\ldots\times 10^{-7}.

Of these nonmixers, exactly 61,931,52061{,}931{,}520 are connected and periodic. The others preserve a nontrivial coset partition. We count every permutation preserving a nontrivial coset partition by the same recurrence at arbitrary dimension. Beginning at six bits, additional primitive permutations can fail to mix. The asymptotic analysis bounds the size of that exceptional family.

Which maps are counted?

Translate the outputs so that p(0)=0p(0)=0. This normalization leaves all difference transitions and invariant coset partitions unchanged and gives N=2nN=2^n original permutations for each normalized one.

Call a subspace WW invariant if pp permutes its cosets. In derivative form, p(x+w)+p(x)∈Wp(x+w)+p(x)\in W for all xx and w∈Ww\in W. A normalized pp is simple here if its only invariant subspaces in this sense are 00 and VV. Equivalently, the group generated by pp and the translations is primitive. The term agrees with simplicity of the algebra (V,+,p,0)(V,+,p,0): its congruence relations are exactly equality modulo such spaces. Published coset criterion, Caranti–Dalla Volta–Sala

Write qnq_n for the number of normalized nonlinear simple permutations and gn=|GL(n,2)|g_n=|\mathrm{GL}(n,2)|, with g0=1g_0=1. The number of simple linear maps is ℓn=gnIn/(2n−1)\ell_n=g_n I_n/(2^n-1) for n>1n>1, where InI_n is the number of monic irreducible binary polynomials of degree nn. Each polynomial gives one conjugacy class and its centralizer consists of the nonzero field multiplications. In dimension one take ℓ1=1\ell_1=1. Thus the exact number of permutations with a proper nonzero invariant coset partition is

(2n)!−2n(qn+ℓn). (2^n)!-2^n(q_n+\ell_n).

At three, four and five bits, the earlier dimension-specific results identify the mixers exactly as the nonlinear simple permutations, up to output translation. In particular, at five bits 25q52^5 q_5 is the full number of mixers. Four-bit proof · Five-bit criterion and its six-bit limit

A signed count from quotient partitions

Let C(p)C(p) be the finite lattice of invariant subspaces. Intersections remain invariant by the derivative criterion. Sums remain invariant by taking successive shifts from the summands. For any such lattice write μ(C)\mu(C) for its Möbius function from bottom to top. In the one-element lattice this value is one.

Use the easily computed numbers

cd=(2d)!−∑j=1d−1[dj]2cj((2d−j)!)2j c_d=(2^d)!-\sum_{j=1}^{d-1}[d\;j]_2 c_j((2^{d-j})!)^{2^j}

from the quotient inclusion–exclusion argument. Here [dj]2[d\;j]_2 counts binary subspaces of codimension jj. The identity we will need is

−cd2d=∑p(0)=0μ(C(p)),d≥1. -\frac{c_d}{2^d}=\sum_{p(0)=0}\mu(C(p)),\qquad d\ge1.

To verify it, before imposing p(0)=0p(0)=0, recall that cdc_d is the signed sum of the numbers of permutations preserving each of a family of proper subspaces with intersection zero. In this definition the zero subspace is allowed. For a fixed permutation the negative of its contribution is the sum of (−1)|F|(-1)^{|F|} over subsets FF of the proper members of C(p)C(p) with meet zero. This is μ(C(p))\mu(C(p)). Indeed for each x<Vx<V, the sum without the meet-zero restriction, over subsets all of whose members contain xx, is zero by the binomial theorem. At x=Vx=V that sum is one. These are exactly the defining equations of the Möbius function after grouping by meet and assigning the empty meet to VV. Output translations divide the total by 2d2^d. This calculation is an application of lattice Möbius inversion. Rota, On the foundations of combinatorial theory I

Why the signed count separates simple nonlinear maps

Splitting when the Möbius value is nonzero. The same binomial argument works using only the maximal proper members of C(p)C(p), because every proper member lies below one. Thus a nonzero Möbius value implies that some family of maximal proper invariant subspaces intersects in zero. Choose an irredundant such family W1,…,WrW_1,\ldots,W_r. For r=1r=1, W1=0W_1=0 and pp is simple. Otherwise set B=⋂i>1WiB=\bigcap_{i>1}W_i. Irredundancy gives B≠0B\ne0; its intersection with W1W_1 is zero, and maximality of W1W_1 then gives V=B⊕W1V=B\oplus W_1. Both coordinate coset partitions are preserved. Normalization implies that pp acts separately on the two coordinates. Its action on BB is the quotient V/W1V/W_1 and is simple.

For each i>1i>1, the map W1→V/WiW_1\to V/W_i is surjective since W1+Wi=VW_1+W_i=V. It intertwines the normalized permutations, so W1∩WiW_1\cap W_i is a maximal proper invariant subspace of W1W_1 by simplicity of this quotient. These kernels intersect in zero. Iterating on W1W_1 gives a direct sum of simple coordinate factors. A permutation without such a decomposition has zero Möbius weight.

A nonlinear simple factor admits no diagonal congruences. Suppose pp acts as (b,y)↦(f(b),h(y))(b,y)\mapsto(f(b),h(y)) on B⊕YB\oplus Y, with ff nonlinear simple. For an invariant space WW, both its projection onto BB and W∩BW\cap B are invariant for ff. For the projection assertion, lift uu in that projection to some (u,v)∈W(u,v)\in W and take the BB coordinate of the derivative. Thus each of those two spaces is either zero or all of BB. If the projection is all of BB and the intersection is zero, fix an arbitrary uu, a lift (u,v)(u,v), and a value of yy. The derivatives based at (b,y)(b,y) and (b′,y)(b',y) both lie in WW and have the same YY coordinate. Their difference lies in W∩B=0W\cap B=0. Hence f(b+u)+f(b)f(b+u)+f(b) is independent of bb for every uu, which would make ff linear since f(0)=0f(0)=0.

It follows that WW either lies in YY or equals B⊕(W∩Y)B\oplus(W\cap Y). All such subspaces with W∩YW\cap Y invariant do occur. The entire lattice is the product of the two-element lattice for BB and the invariant lattice for YY. Repeating this for all nonlinear factors makes their coordinate subspaces intrinsic: they are precisely the minimal nonzero invariant subspaces on which the restriction is nonlinear. The complementary linear summand is intrinsic as well, since the split lattice shows that it contains every invariant subspace with linear restriction. Thus different unordered decompositions into nonlinear simple factors and one remaining linear summand yield distinct permutations. General results on congruences of products in Mal'cev varieties provide context for the elementary argument above. Mayr–Ruškuc, Lemma 3.3 and the proof of Theorem 4.2

The signed linear mass. Let LL range over the invertible linear maps on an mm-space. Sum the alternating-chain formula for μ(C(L))\mu(C(L)) over these maps. For a chain 0=U0<U1<⋯<Ur=V0=U_0<U_1<\cdots<U_r=V with fixed intermediate dimensions, the sum over all such flags of the sizes of their stabilizers is gmg_m by orbit–stabilizer. Its sign is (−1)r(-1)^r. There are (m−1r−1)\binom{m-1}{r-1} dimension patterns. Hence the sum over LL vanishes for m≥2m\ge2, equals −1-1 for m=1m=1, and equals 11 for m=0m=0.

The exact recurrence

Möbius functions multiply on direct products of finite lattices, immediately from their defining equations. A decomposition with rr simple nonlinear factors and a remaining linear map LL has weight (−1)rμ(C(L))(-1)^r\mu(C(L)). Every map with nonzero weight is counted by such decompositions. Allowing arbitrary LL includes any additional maps with zero weight automatically.

Suppose there are kdk_d nonlinear factors of dimension dd and the linear summand has dimension m=n−∑ddkdm=n-\sum_d d k_d. The number of decompositions into these actual coordinate subspaces, without an ordering among the nonlinear factors of each dimension, is

gngm∏dgdkdkd!. \frac{g_n}{g_m\prod_d g_d^{k_d} k_d!}.

This follows from transitivity of the general linear group on decompositions. There are qdq_d choices of normalized nonlinear simple permutation on each specified dd-space. Summing over the multiplicities is exactly the formal power series identity

1−∑n≥1cnzn2ngn=(1−z)exp(−∑n≥1qngnzn). 1-\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{c_n z^n}{2^n g_n} =(1-z)\exp\left(-\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{q_n}{g_n}z^n\right).

This formal coefficient identity computes all qnq_n successively. The exponential for unordered labeled direct summands is the classical finite-vector-space exponential formula. The factor 1−z1-z comes from the signed linear mass computed above. Morrison, Theorem 8

For an explicit rational-arithmetic version, set ad=cd/(2dgd)a_d=c_d/(2^d g_d) and

Rd=dad+∑j=1d−1ajRd−j,qd=gdd(Rd−1). R_d=d a_d+\sum_{j=1}^{d-1}a_j R_{d-j},\qquad q_d=\frac{g_d}{d}(R_d-1).

These equations follow by taking the logarithmic derivative. All truth tables on two bits fixing zero are linear. Thus q1=q2=0q_1=q_2=0. Up to dimension five there is room for at most one simple nonlinear factor. Since the signed linear mass vanishes beyond dimension one, in this range the recurrence simplifies to

qn=cn2n+(2n−1)2n−1qn−1,3≤n≤5. q_n=\frac{c_n}{2^n}+(2^n-1)2^{n-1} q_{n-1},\qquad 3\le n\le5.

The second term counts the choices of a nonlinear hyperplane factor and a complementary line. Evaluating the recurrence gives the following exact checks and result.

Bits Permutations preserving a nontrivial coset partition Pairwise mixers

The three-bit census and the earlier four-bit color-partition count provide independent checks. The exact five-bit fraction also falls within the independently obtained parity-based bounds. One can exhaustively check the small-dimensional inputs to the signed argument without enumerating 32!32! permutations. The test suite constructs the complete invariant lattice for all 5,040 normalized three-bit tables and checks the nonlinear product argument against all 2,825 binary subspaces of a six-bit example.
